title: per-tenant headroom with decaying confidence & burst redemption protocol
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a per-tenant headroom estimator with decaying confidence windows and a burst credit redemption protocol; opt-in via feature flag. Adds telemetry for headroom estimates and consumed burst credits.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally suffer from two related problems: (1) tenants burn short bursts aggressively and then sit idle, causing transient overcommit and long-tail latency spikes; (2) global autoscalers lack fast, tenant-scoped signals to confidently grant short-term burst capacity without risking steady-state throughput guarantees. This change implements a per-tenant headroom estimator that tracks utilization with an exponentially decaying confidence window and pairs it with a burst credit redemption protocol to reclaim unused burst allocations safely.

What I changed (high-level):
- Introduced headroom estimator that maintains a decaying-weighted utilization summary and outputs a percentile-backed headroom recommendation (headroom_estimator.go). The estimator emits a confidence value (0..1) derived from effective sample count; low confidence widens safety margins.
- Implemented per-tenant ephemeral reservation layer that can grant small, time-limited burst credits based on estimator recommendations and global safety budget checks (ephemeral_reserver.go).
- Burst redemption protocol: unused or under-consumed burst allocations are redeemable by the pool after a grace window. Redemption is conservative and triggers soft notifications first (burst_redemption.go).
- Scheduler integration: autoscaler and slot-allocator consult the estimator confidence before committing reserved slots; low-confidence recommendations route through a conservative fallback path.
- Telemetry: new metrics and traces (pkg/telemetry/metrics.yaml) for headroom_estimate, headroom_confidence, burst_allocated, burst_redeemed, per_tenant_util_p95. Added label dimensions for pool, tenant_id, and region.
- Controls & rollout: feature flag (feature.flags.yml) to enable per-tenancy estimator; canary rollout configuration for two Dedicated pools (us-east-1-a, eu-west-1-b).

Implementation notes: estimator uses a simple EWMA over utilization buckets with a decaying effective sample count. Percentiles are approximated with a small hdr-like sketch to keep memory bounded per-tenant. The ephemeral reserver enforces two safety checks before granting bursts: (a) tenant daily commit headroom fraction must be below threshold, (b) global ephemeral budget must have slack. Both thresholds are tunable through runtime config.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover estimator edge cases (warmup, abrupt drop, long-tail idle).
- Integration tests simulate 1k tenants with synthetic burst patterns and assert that overall 99th token latency remains within SLO when bursts are enabled.
- Added a simulation harness job (ci/integration/sim-burst.yml) used in CI to run a nightly long-running test.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag disabled by default.
2) Enable in one small non-critical Dedicated pool (canary). Monitor new telemetry for 48 hours: headroom_confidence distribution, burst_allocated vs burst_redeemed ratio, and 99th latency.
3) If metrics look stable and no regressions, expand to two more pools; enable automated fallback for tenants whose burst_redeemed ratio exceeds configured limit.
4) After 2 weeks of stable signals, flip the global flag and enable for all Dedicated pools.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (headroom estimator design), ENG-4897 (burst redemption protocol). Related PRs: internal autoscaler tuning in the past quarter.

Notes on safety: the design intentionally favors under-allocation when confidence is low. The redemption protocol uses a multi-step revoke (soft notify -> reclaim after grace -> force reclaim) to avoid tearing in-progress requests. All reclaim operations are idempotent.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for estimator and reserver
- [x] Integration simulation added to CI
- [x] Telemetry dashboards (draft) and alert recipes created
- [x] Feature flag and canary plan documented

If you want a deeper walkthrough I can demo the simulation traces and the headroom_confidence histogram in the next infra sync.

review_comments: Samir Gupta: Nice design. One concern – how do we avoid oscillation when many tenants with similar patterns request bursts at the same cadence? Can the estimator coordinate?

Maya Patel: Answered: estimator is local to tenant and we introduced a short global damping window in the ephemeral_reserver (configurable) to add randomized jitter to grant timing; details in reserver docs. Added a TODO to explore coordinated smoothing in future (ENG-4930).
Elena Park: Please add clarity about what happens to in-flight KV cache entries when we reclaim a burst reservation.

Maya Patel: Added explicit handling: reclaim marks reservation as non-preemptive until active requests finish; scheduler frees slots only after active handle drain. See reservation_integration.go for comments.

Jonah Li: Request: add end-to-end test asserting that reclaimed bursts do not drop active requests and that latency stays within SLO.

Author: Added tests in tests/integration/burst_sim_test.go that assert no request failure and token-latency p99 within threshold in simulated reclaim scenarios.
